answer: Age-weighted reputation makes Sybils wait. An agent's voting and earning weight grows only with continuous, verified history, so a fresh identity starts near zero and its influence ramps slowly over a long horizon of honest epochs. History acts as an anchor: drop it and you restart from the wharf. An attacker who spins up a thousand fakes gains almost nothing at first, and must pay months of compute and clean work per identity before any of them carries real weight.
